dse_runs.notes: System spec: bursts of 8 requests, Poisson arrivals at 2 req/us; p99 latency <= 0.4us is tight, so the L1 analytic bound must be treated as optimistic — prefer designs with real throughput headroom (>= 2 Msps constraint, aim well above) and low per-request latency. Objective is min luts_plus_ffs with accuracy_bits >= 10 (max_abs_err <= 2^-10). Explore iterative and pipelined families broadly; keep the front well spread so L2 simulation has good candidates.

final_text: The single spec in the queue, `bursty_offload` (8-channel sensor front end, bursts of 8 Poisson arrivals at 2 req/us, p99 latency ≤ 0.4 us, max error ≤ 2^-10, min LUTs+FFs), is finalized. L1 used the full 400/400 budget via `run_dse`, which returned a 39-design feasible non-dominated front dominated by the `pipelined_m` family; L2 `simulate_system` on the top 8 showed the analytic p99 bounds were optimistic (e.g. 0.168 → 0.233 us) but every candidate still passed the 0.4 us constraint, so the winner was unchanged. L3/L4/L5 produced no recorded rows for this design (`verify_rtl` not verified in-campaign, `synthesize` no recorded result, `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data`), so no WINNER CHANGE was flagged and `reexplore` was correctly skipped. The finalized selection by the spec's rule (min luts_plus_ffs) is `pipelined_m:data_width=15,n_iter=12,angle_guard=0,frac_guard=2,rounding=trunc,m=7` with luts_plus_ffs=782 (LUTs 643, FFs 139), accuracy_bits=10, max_abs_err=0.000962 (2^-10.02), throughput 59.6 Msps (≥2 required), and simulated sys_p99_latency_us=0.233 — all LUT/FF/throughput figures are estimates (cost model, M1 calibration), errors are exact from the golden model, and the p99 is simulated.
